summary: How Tech Works: watched 4 published Shorts and the newest one. Added one lesson (the second line answers, it never asks again) and queued one look test.
why: All four Shorts with a curve lose the most at 5-8 s, on the line after the hook. In three of them that line asked the question again: transistor -23 points at 6.2 s, Hoover Dam -18.5 at 7.5 s (stayed 47.4%, 10.5 under the 57.9% median), Crossrail -15.4 at 5.6 s.

findings.title: The second beat is where viewers leave
findings.detail: Microwave -29.6 points at 7.5 s ('In 1945, radar engineer Percy Spencer...'), transistor -23 at 6.2 s ('What did the very first one look like?'), Hoover Dam -18.5 at 7.5 s ('So how does water make power?'), Crossrail -15.4 at 5.6 s.

findings.title: One machine in one place held best
findings.detail: Crossrail held 46.5% after the hook, staying on one tunnel machine; the Shorts that cut between six or seven places held 10.7-26.4%.

findings.title: Newest Short repeats the pattern
findings.detail: v-20261123-21 (Motorola brick) opens its second line on backstory ('Its engineers had just 6 weeks...'); its curve gets checked Friday.

changes.title: Lesson added: the second line answers, it never asks again
Challenger queued: tech-one-machine-one-place
changes.detail: Look test judged on held after the hook; also added Crossrail's curve to research's tech-mechanism-by-6s.
